import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_1.csv"
    
    # Load Source 0: user ratings data
    # Schema: ['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
    df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    
    # Load Source 1: movie metadata
    # Schema includes ['item_id', 'movie title', ...]
    df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    
    # We want to join Source0 and Source1 on 'item_id' to get the movie title for each rating
    # Source0 has 50,000 rows, Source1 has 1,682 rows
    
    # Select only needed columns from Source1 to reduce memory usage
    df_source1_reduced = df_source1[['item_id', 'movie title']]
    
    # Merge on 'item_id' (inner join to keep only ratings with known movie titles)
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1_reduced, on='item_id', how='inner')
    
    # Ensure the target schema and types:
    # Target Schema: ['user_id': int, 'item_id': int, 'rating': int, 'timestamp': int, 'movie title': str]
    df_merged = df_merged.astype({
        'user_id': 'int32',
        'item_id': 'int32',
        'rating': 'int32',
        'timestamp': 'int64',  # timestamp can be large, use int64
        'movie title': 'string'
    })
    
    # The target table name is Target1_42, but since we export to CSV, we just save the dataframe
    
    # Export the result to the specified path
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    df_merged.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
    
    print(f"Transformation complete. Output saved to {output_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
